page: Microsoft Azure FX96mds_v2 is a high-frequency, compute and memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 260 MB of L3 cache, support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, and comes paired with 1832.0 GB of system memory, providing 19.08 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and contains no discrete GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the FX96mds_v2 demonstrates strong multi-core computational throughput and high memory bandwidth. The system achieves a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 103610.4 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 97945.78, supported by top-tier results in extended vector instructions and encryption tests. Memory throughput reaches 444.43 GB/sec in uncached reads and 188.83 GB/sec in uncached writes. These metrics translate to high operational throughput in memory-bound services, producing 130.32 million Redis SET operations per second and 145.38 GB/sec in static web serving.

Given its 4.2 GHz clock speed, massive memory pool, and integrated NVMe storage, the FX96mds_v2 is configured for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput database operations, and intensive data processing. Cost efficiency is driven by high resource density on a single node, which reduces network overhead for large datasets via local NVMe storage. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its application for accelerated deep learning workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure FX96mds_v2 is a high-frequency compute and memory-focused virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores and 260 MB of L3 cache, it supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance pairs this high-frequency compute capacity with 1832.0 GB of memory and 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, operating without dedicated GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution, delivering 103610.4 in PassMark CPU tests, 444.43 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth, and 130.32 million Redis SET operations per second. The server provides dense resource consolidation for single-node scaling, presenting a viable hardware profile for large in-memory databases, database operations, caching layers, and high-throughput CPU-driven batch processing requiring extensive local scratch storage.
